question: Will the House Energy & Commerce Committee begin a markup on the Trahan–Obernolte comprehensive AI framework (or a bill derived from the Great American AI Act) on September 17 or 18, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is NO: as of 2026-09-08 the E&C site shows only two subcommittee hearings for Sept 15 and no markup notice for Sept 17-18, while House leadership canceled the Sept 21 and Sept 28 weeks, leaving roughly four session days (Mon Sept 14 - Thu Sept 17) and making Friday Sept 18 effectively dead. E&C practice is to announce markups by press release ~5-8 days ahead with text posted 24-48h prior; nothing has appeared, so a YES requires an announcement in the next few days for the final getaway-week day. Chairman Guthrie remains publicly noncommittal on any comprehensive AI bill before the election, and the committee's revealed choice on Sept 1 was to advance narrow AI bills (explicitly excluded by the fine print) rather than the Trahan-Obernolte framework, whose state-preemption title is the most contested piece. The GAAIA-derived vehicle does exist (H.R. 9925 FRONTIER Act, introduced July 23, referred to E&C), and sponsors are pushing hard with a now-or-never window, which is the main YES pathway; but P(any GAAIA-derived markup that week) looks like a single-digit percentage and only part of that lands on Sept 17-18 specifically. No prediction market prices this contract.
